facts.raw_span: A 58-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of a right-breast lump
no family history of breast cancer
had been menopausal for 5 years
denied eating frogs or snakes
recalled drinking impure water
migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
a mobile lump was palpated
a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity, measuring 5.0 × 1.7 × 0.7 cm (BIRADS 4b)
an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, measuring 1.8 × 1.2 × 0.4 cm (BIRADS 4a) and closely abutting the pectoralis major
two small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer, measuring 0.5 × 0.3 cm and 0.3 × 0.2 cm
No obvious blood-flow signals were detected within any of these lesions on color Doppler flow imaging

no family history of breast cancer

recalled drinking impure water
migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
a mobile lump was palpated
a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity, measuring 5.0 × 1.7 × 0.7 cm (BIRADS 4b)
an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, measuring 1.8 × 1.2 × 0.4 cm (BIRADS 4a) and closely abutting the pectoralis major
two small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer, measuring 0.5 × 0.3 cm and 0.3 × 0.2 cm
No obvious blood-flow signals were detected within any of these lesions on color Doppler flow imaging

concepts.why: The presence of a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity and an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, both with high BIRADS scores, suggests invasive ductal carcinoma.
The mobile lump and small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer could be consistent with fibroadenoma, a common benign breast tumor.

The hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity and the oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours could also be consistent with a phyllodes tumor, a rare breast tumor.
The small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer could also represent breast cysts, which are common and usually benign.
The presence of a hypoechoic, tubular structure and an oval, low-echo mass could also suggest papillary carcinoma, a rare type of breast cancer.

rationales.F08: The presence of a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity is highly suggestive of a malignant lesion, such as invasive ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F09: The presence of an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours is highly suggestive of a malignant lesion, such as invasive ductal carcinoma or papillary carcinoma.
